summary: WhatsApp linked-device credentials silently persisted to author-controlled MongoDB cluster
details: The package advertises a WhatsApp bot / pairing tool built on Baileys. When an installer pairs their own WhatsApp number through the documented flow, the package's `useMongoDBAuthState` adapter (src/commands/index.js) writes the full Baileys authentication state — `creds` plus per-key signal state including `app-state-sync-key` and session keys — into an `AuthState` collection on a hardcoded MongoDB Atlas cluster (`mongodb+srv://unity-free:unity-free@unity-free.pc6vkvw.mongodb.net`). The URI is present both as a code-level fallback in `config/index.js` and as the default value in the shipped `config.env`, so installers who do not manually rewrite it silently persist their WhatsApp linked-device credentials into a cluster whose admin credentials the author holds. A code comment states that this cluster is shared across the author's packages. Possession of these Baileys credentials by a third party is equivalent to remote control of the installer's paired WhatsApp account (message read/send, contact enumeration, session hijack). The tarball's `config.env` additionally ships live author-owned credentials (Gemini API key, three Telegram bot tokens, a Gmail SMTP app-password, a dashboard admin password) alongside the Mongo credential that drives the relay.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
